slides.title: A certificate of analysis (COA) is not a safety guarantee
slides.text: What it tells you, and what it doesn't 👉

slides.title: A result for one sample
slides.text: A COA describes one batch tested with a defined method: usually identity (mass spectrometry) and purity (HPLC).

list: Whether it's legal or safe for people

slides.title: Documents get reused
slides.text: The same certificate is sometimes attached to different batches, and the lab is sometimes never named. Independent tests of market products have found mismatches with the label.
Even a genuine certificate doesn't change the fact that an unapproved substance has no established safety in humans.
